text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
- Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland, in his first election year debate against conservative leader Jan Petersen, said working for more equality in society is a central task in politics.

- A majority in parliament wants to offer sexual criminals "chemical castration" by means of special therapy that blocks the male hormone testosteron. But uncertainty prevails on how to proceed with the proposal.

- Aage Korsvold, top executive of insurance company Storebrand, is very annoyed that industrial group Aker RGI ASA has sown doubt about whether the insurer is capable of redeeming preference shares as pledged.
- Fidelity International has reduced its stake in Norwegian shares by 36 percent in the past year, but remains the largest foreign investor on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
- Oil worth 1.6 billion crowns will be lost if parliament delays the construction of the Troll C platform.

- A conflict has broken out between top executive Aage Korsvold of insurer Storebrand and billionaire investor Kjell Inge Roekke of Aker RGI after Aker RGI's remarks about the validity of Storebrand's preference shares.
- While southern Norway can expect a slight increase in the number of foreign tourists this summer, northern Norway looks headed for its third summer with dwindling tourism.
- There are several indications that the Rasmussen Group in Kristiansand will be the partner Statoil is looking for in its shipping business.
- Petroleum Geo-Services was very pleased with its first-quarter results, which grew to $9.9 million in pre-tax profits from $4.0 million in the corresponding 1996 quarter.

- The game is over for Fokus Bank Managing Director Bjarne Borgersen. His attempt to merge with mortgage lender BNbank has been undermined by rival bidder Den norske Bank buying stock in Fokus. Den norske Bank thus wants to ensure that it acquires BNbank by blocking Fokus' attempts.
